title: Multidevice compatibility sweep and triage for UI Kit tokens, controls, and charts
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Scope: Run a focused compatibility sweep across Safari (macOS & iOS), Firefox (desktop & Android), and a representative set of mobile viewports for the UI Kit. Target surface areas: design tokens (color, spacing, typography), buttons (variants, disabled/focus state), table stripe/pagination/layout, and chart rendering (axis labels, tooltips, canvas vs SVG fallbacks).

Goals:
- Identify visual regressions and interaction bugs that diverge from the reference spec in Figma.
- Categorize failures into visual regressions, accessibility regressions (contrast/focus), and functional regressions (broken touch targets, clipping, overflow).
- Produce a prioritized bug queue with reproduction steps, screenshots, environment matrix, and suggested fixes (token change vs runtime workaround).
- Recommend quick-win patches for upcoming release ui-kit-2026.03 and longer-term process improvements (QA checklist, automated visual diffs).

Acceptance criteria:
- At least one verified reproduction for each unique bug with screenshots from two browser/device combos.
- Triage items assigned with severity and owner, and 70% of P0/P1 items either fixed or scoped into eng tickets before release cut.
- A short playbook describing how to run the compatibility sweep and add new viewports to the matrix.

Approach/Notes:
- Use Figma reference frames pinned to token values as ground truth. For charts, compare canvas/SVG rendering against a headless render to detect label clipping.
- Prioritize tokens that affect multiple components first (eg. spacing-xs, neutral-600).
- Mobile testing uses Pixel 6 (Chrome/Firefox), iPhone 13 Safari, and iPad Safari for touch/hover variations.
- We'll run a small automated visual-diff job (Chromatic/Backstop prototype) for desktop Chrome to reduce noise; manual checks for Safari/Firefox.

Tradeoffs and constraints:
- Full cross-browser automation for Safari is fragile; rely on manual verification for Safari/IOS for now.
- Some chart regressions are upstream in the charting library; we'll flag as dependency rather than immediate UI Kit changes when appropriate.
